inline_comments.comment: `CHANGE_DETECTION_STATUS_TYPE_ID` is imported from `'./service'`, but `service.ts` imports that constant from `'storybook/internal/types'` — it never re-exports it. This is a compile-time error that would prevent the test file from building. Change the import to `'storybook/internal/types'` (or re-export the constant from `service.ts` if callers are expected to obtain it from there).

The `enabled === false` strict-equality check means change detection runs whenever `enabled` is `undefined` — i.e., whenever the caller passes `features?.changeDetection` and the user has not set the flag. The feature type declares `@default false`, but with this guard an unconfigured project silently becomes a participant. The check should be `if (!enabled)` (or the call-site in `dev-server.ts` should supply an explicit fallback: `features?.changeDetection ?? false`) so that the opt-in semantics match the documented default.

`indexGenerator` is used immediately after `presets.apply()` with no null/undefined guard. Per the project rule, the result of `presets.apply()` must be validated before use; if the `storyIndexGenerator` preset is absent the call returns `undefined` and `.getIndex()` on the next line throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined`. Add an explicit runtime guard — e.g. `if (!indexGenerator) { logger.warn('Change detection: storyIndexGenerator preset unavailable'); return; }` — before calling `.getIndex()`.

`changeDetectionService.dispose()` is only called in the preview-builder error path; the normal `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` shutdown handler (`cancelTelemetry`) does not dispose the service. This leaves the debounce timer and the `onModuleGraphChange` subscription alive until the process exits. Dispose in the SIGINT/SIGTERM handler or in the `cancelTelemetry` callback so resources are cleaned up on graceful shutdown.

Commented-out debug statement (`// logger.info(\`Story ${entry.id} absolute path: ${absolutePath}\`);`) should be removed before merging. Per project guidelines, commented-out code must either be deleted entirely or replaced with a `// TODO:` that names the reason it is disabled and when it will be re-enabled.

`dispose()` clears `debounceTimer` and calls `unsubscribe`, but does not reset `this.rerunAfterCurrentScan`. If a scan is in-flight when `dispose()` is called and `rerunAfterCurrentScan` is already `true`, the `finally` block of `scan()` will dispatch `void this.scan()` after disposal, causing the service to mutate the status store after it has been torn down. Set `this.rerunAfterCurrentScan = false` inside `dispose()` (and consider adding an `isDisposed` guard at the top of `scan()`) to prevent post-disposal writes.

`changeDetection: true` is committed to the shared `.storybook/main.ts`. The feature type documents `@default false` with a TODO to flip it before the 10.4 release, which means this opt-in line in the shared dev config is a developer-era testing override. Per project rules, developer-specific values should not be committed to shared config files — drive this via an environment variable (`process.env.STORYBOOK_CHANGE_DETECTION`) or a git-ignored local override instead. If keeping it is intentional (e.g., to dog-food the feature during development), add an inline comment explaining that this will be removed before release.

general_comments.comment: The module-level singleton pattern in `readiness.ts` (`readinessDeferred` / `readinessState`) combined with the instance-level `readinessResolved` flag in `ChangeDetectionService` creates a subtle inconsistency: if `resetChangeDetectionReadiness()` is called on the module (e.g., for an in-process server restart) the module-level deferred is refreshed, but the still-alive service instance has `readinessResolved = true` and will silently refuse to push any further updates. Since `resetChangeDetectionReadiness()` is called inside the constructor, a new instance must be created for each server lifecycle — confirm that `dev-server.ts` constructs a fresh `ChangeDetectionService` on restart (rather than reusing an existing one) or the readiness state will be permanently stale after the first restart.

The `features` block type in `StorybookConfigRaw` documents `changeDetection` with `@default false`, but the runtime behavior (the `enabled === false` check in `ChangeDetectionService.start`) treats `undefined` as "enabled". The TODO comment says "Turn to true before 10.4 release", implying the intent is to flip the default — but that flip should happen in the common preset (as required by project rules for opt-out feature flags), not by quietly relying on `undefined !== false`. Either honour the current `@default false` semantics now (use `!enabled` or supply `?? false` at the call-site) or explicitly set the default to `true` in the common preset and update the JSDoc.
